transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I suppose what finally brought me in is that... I just feel like the part of me that used to reach out for people, or take any pleasure in my work, has gone very quiet. I mean, I'm a social worker, so you'd think I'd be more on top of this, but... I used to really care. And yoga, too. I used to go to this studio over on 4th Street. It’s right next to this little bakery that makes the most incredible almond croissants. The woman who works the counter, I think her name is Elise, she has this bright red hair and she always remembers my order. I haven't seen her in a while, though. 

I haven't been to the art galleries either, or even opened my journal in... I don't know how long. I used to write every morning with my coffee. My favorite mug has a little chip on the handle, but I can't bring myself to throw it away because my niece made it for me at one of those paint-your-own pottery places for my birthday a few years ago. She painted a little wonky yellow sun on it. 

But anyway... yeah, the journaling and everything else, it's just stopped. I’m mostly just moving through my obligations these days. Just waking up and doing what I have to do.
About how long have you been feeling this way?

It’s been about eight months. This whole change in how I’m thinking, working, and connecting with people... it really all started right around the time we took my older relative into our apartment. 

Which, honestly, was a massive adjustment just physically. We had to completely clear out the second bedroom, and I had all my old graduate school textbooks stored in there. I mean, I don't know why I hold onto them, the field changes so much anyway, but you just feel terrible throwing away a book that heavy, you know? We ended up having to rent a little storage unit over on Route 9 for all my boxes. It's right next to that huge car dealership, the one that always has those giant inflatable wavy-arm guys out front? I always wonder who actually invented those things, they're oddly mesmerizing when you're stuck in traffic next to them. 

But... wait, what was I saying? Oh, right, the timeline. Yeah, it's been about eight months since they moved in.
Have you ever experienced a period like this before in your life?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I was stressed, sure, but nothing like this where everything just feels... muted. Actually, speaking of muted, the TV in our living room has been doing this weird thing where the sound just cuts out randomly. My husband thinks it's a loose cable, but I swear it only happens when we're watching those cooking shows. Do you ever watch those? The baking championships? I always feel so bad for the contestants when their sugar sculptures collapse. It takes so much patience to work with spun sugar. I tried making caramel once for a flan, and I completely burned it. The smell lingered in the kitchen for days. We had to keep the windows open, which was awful because it was right in the middle of pollen season. The yellow dust was just coating everything on the porch... 

But, um, no, to answer your question, this feeling... it's new for me. I've never had a stretch like this before.
Have you ever had a period in your life where you felt the complete opposite—unusually energetic, wired, or needing very little sleep without feeling tired?

No, I've never had anything like that. I've always been a pretty solid sleeper, honestly. Eight hours a night, like clockwork. My husband, though, he's a terrible sleeper. He tosses and turns all night, and he has this CPAP machine that makes this rhythmic whooshing sound. It's supposed to be quiet, but to me, it sounds exactly like the ocean. Which you'd think would be relaxing, right? Like one of those white noise machines. We actually bought one of those for our niece when she was a baby, one that projected little stars onto the ceiling. It was so cute. They lived in this tiny apartment in the city back then, right above a Thai restaurant, so the white noise was essential because of the street traffic and the smell of pad thai wafting up at all hours. I love Thai food, especially drunken noodles. There's a place downtown that makes the best drunken noodles, they put just the right amount of Thai basil in it. I tried growing basil on my windowsill once, but I think I overwatered it because the leaves all turned yellow and fell off. I just don't have a green thumb, I guess. 

But no, I've never felt wired or like I didn't need sleep. Just the opposite lately, really.
Aside from losing interest in activities, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless?

No, not really sad or hopeless. Just... flat, I guess. Like everything is just kind of gray. Which is funny because I used to love painting. Watercolors, mostly. I took a class at the community center a few years ago with this instructor who was just so passionate about color theory. He made us spend an entire week just mixing different shades of blue. Cobalt, ultramarine, cerulean... it's amazing how many blues there are when you really look. I actually painted a seascape for my sister's birthday, and she hung it in her guest bathroom. It matched her towels perfectly. She gets all her towels from this little boutique downtown that imports them from Turkey. They're incredibly soft, but they take absolutely forever to dry in the dryer. Our dryer has been acting up lately, actually, it keeps squeaking on the spin cycle. I told my husband we should just get a new one, but he insists he can fix it if he just watches enough YouTube tutorials. He fixed the toaster that way once, though it still smells a little like burning plastic when you use the bagel setting... 

But, um, anyway, no. I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. Just... not really feeling much of anything.
Have you been feeling fatigued or experiencing a significant lack of energy nearly every day?

I wouldn't say I'm physically tired, no. I mean, I'm not exhausted or anything. I just don't really have the drive to do much. It's more of a mental thing, I think. Like, I have the energy to get up and go to work, but once I'm there... I'm a social worker, by the way. Have I mentioned that? I work mostly with substance abuse cases. It's usually a lot of paperwork, which I used to not mind so much. I actually like organizing files. I bought this label maker last month, one of those digital ones where you can change the font? I spent a whole Saturday labeling all the pantry shelves. Spices, baking goods, canned vegetables... I even labeled the dog treat jar. We have a golden retriever mix, Buster. He's such a good boy, but he sheds everywhere. I have to vacuum every single day, sometimes twice a day if it's shedding season. We bought one of those robot vacuums to help, but Buster is terrified of it. He barks at it the whole time it's running, so it kind of defeats the purpose of it being convenient. My husband thinks it's hilarious, he actually recorded a video of Buster barking at it and sent it to his brother in Ohio. His brother has three dogs, so he gets it. They live out in the country, though, so the dogs just run around outside all day. I'd love to have a big yard like that someday...

But, no, I'm not really fatigued. Just... lacking motivation, I guess.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight lately?

Not really, no. I eat about the same as I always do, and my clothes all fit exactly the same. We usually do our grocery shopping on Sunday mornings, right when the store opens so it's not too crowded. But they completely rearranged the aisles at our local place last week. It was so frustrating. I spent twenty minutes just trying to find the coffee. They moved it all the way to the back near the dairy, which makes absolutely no sense to me. I like to buy whole beans and grind them myself. My husband got me this really nice burr grinder for Christmas a couple of years ago. It has all these different settings, from coarse for French press to super fine for espresso. I don't really drink espresso, though, it's a bit too strong for me. We went to Italy for our honeymoon, and everyone there drinks espresso standing up at these little bars. It's such a different culture. The architecture there is just stunning, especially in Florence. We climbed to the top of the Duomo and the view was incredible, even though the stairs were so narrow and steep... I think I had to stop and catch my breath like three times on the way up. 

But anyway, yeah, my appetite is totally normal. No weight changes or anything like that.
How has your sleep been over these past few months?

My sleep? It's fine, I think. I haven't really noticed any changes. I usually go to bed around ten thirty. We always watch the late local news first, mostly just to see the weather forecast. The meteorologist they have on channel four is so dramatic, though. Whenever there's even a chance of rain, he acts like it's a hurricane. It reminds me of when we lived in Florida for a couple of years for my husband's job. The thunderstorms there are incredible, just rolling in every afternoon at exactly three o'clock. You could set your watch by them. We had this screened-in lanai at that house, and I loved sitting out there listening to the rain on the metal roof. It was so peaceful. The only problem was the humidity, it completely ruined my hair. I tried every anti-frizz serum on the market, but nothing worked. I finally just started wearing it in a braid most days. I actually learned how to do a French braid from this girl in my college dorm. She was from Louisiana and had the thickest, most gorgeous hair I've ever seen. We used to stay up half the night just talking and doing each other's hair... 

But, um, sleep. Yeah, my sleep is completely normal. No issues there.
